title: Sales Enablement: Unified Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing, Pitch Decks, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook equips SDRs, AEs, solution engineers, and enablement partners with an opinionated, repeatable narrative and asset set for positioning Redwood Inference to prospects. It bundles messaging by buyer persona, concise competitive counters, a pitch-deck narrative, pricing guidance and a short security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations. Use this as the single source of truth for customer-facing materials and objections handling.

Scope: Target: engineering and ML platform buyers (startup/scale to enterprise); use-cases: chat & assistant features, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embeddings at scale, ingest-and-serve LLM features with enterprise SLAs.

1) Positioning & Core Messaging

Headline (elevator): Redwood Inference: predictable, economical LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — built for production.

Three-minute pitch (engineer-centric):
- Problem: Model quality is improving rapidly, but serving is where teams spend time and money — building reliable, low-latency, cost-effective inference is operationally hard.
- Solution: Redwood provides a unified runtime and control plane that standardizes inference across hosted API, reserved (Dedicated) GPU pools, and private on-prem/VPC deployments — with tooling for cost optimization, observability, and safe rollouts.
- Why now: Open models + specialized inference primitives mean teams can reduce model spend but must invest in serving. Redwood removes that burden and gives predictable unit economics.

Positioning pillars (talk to these in every deck):
- Production-first: latency SLOs, 99.9% SLA options for Dedicated customers, robust fallback and canary rollouts to prevent downtime.
- Unified deployment: switch between hosted, dedicated, and private without rewriting your integration.
- Cost-aware controls: batching, KV/prefix cache, quantization profiles, and routing policies with transparent token-level breakdowns.
- Developer-first: simple REST/SDK, streaming, function/tool calling, and model catalog with performance profiles.

Buyer-focused messaging (one-liners):
- Platform/Infrastructure lead: "Standardize inference across teams with predictable cost, capacity, and SLAs — reduce duplicated ops work and hardware fragmentation."
- Product/ML lead: "Ship LLM features faster with consistent performance and built-in evals to catch regressions before they reach users."
- Security/Compliance lead: "Deploy on VPC or on-prem with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs for sensitive workloads."

2) Competitive Briefs (summary + 1-line counterpoints)

Competitor: General cloud AI endpoints (major cloud providers)
- Strengths: Deep infra integration, global regions.
- Redwood counter: We provide model-focused optimizations (kernel selection, continuous batching, KV cache) and an opinionated runtime tuned for inference economics — plus consistent cross-deployment APIs that cloud endpoints don’t standardize.

Competitor: LLM API providers (simplicity-focused)
- Strengths: Simple developer UX.
- Redwood counter: We match developer ergonomics while delivering predictable throughput, fine-grain cost controls, and enterprise-grade Dedicated/Private options. For customers where cost & SLA matter, Redwood reduces unit economics and operational burden.

Competitor: Self-hosted inference runtimes / infra vendors
- Strengths: Full control and on-prem freedom.
- Redwood counter: We offer a hybrid: private deployments with a Redwood control plane or fully private packages plus best-in-class serving runtime optimizations and operational tooling — saves build time and improves consistency.

Objection handling — common asks and short scripts:
- "We can run models ourselves cheaper." → "If you include engineering time, reliability risk, and missed optimizations (KV caching, kernel selection, batching), the real TCO often favors Redwood — and we accelerate time-to-value with validated configs and rollouts."
- "We need an on-prem solution." → "Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem bundles with KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, and customer-managed networking. We run an on-prem packaging kit and onboarding playbook for regulated workloads."

3) Pitch Deck Narrative (slide-by-slide one-liners)

- Slide 1: Title — Customer name + ‘Production LLMs with predictable economics’
- Slide 2: Problem — Bullet examples of failed in-house inference projects: cost overruns, unpredictable latency, fragmented infra.
- Slide 3: Market/Timing — growth in open models & latency-sensitive apps; inference is the new bottleneck.
- Slide 4: Redwood solution — diagram: client → Redwood API/runtime → Dedicated/Private options → metrics/observability.
- Slide 5: Key differentiators — production-first runtime, unified API across deployment modes, cost controls, rollouts/evals.
- Slide 6: SLA & reliability — target SLOs, redundancy patterns, canary flow.
- Slide 7: Pricing & commercial options — self-serve hosted, reserved Dedicated, Private licensing. (See pricing table)
- Slide 8: Case studies — 2 short examples (below).
- Slide 9: Security & compliance — bullet on VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO assessments where applicable.
- Slide 10: Next steps & CTA — trial, pilot scope, success criteria (latency, cost per 1M tokens, integration milestones).

Slide tips for AE/SEs: keep technical slides visual (sequence diagrams), include sample latency/cost charts from our benchmark suite, and always show a recommended pilot (two-week integration + 4-week performance/ops pilot).

4) Pricing Guidance (talk track + simple tier table)

Commercial options:
- Hosted API (self-serve) — pay-as-you-go per-token and per-embedding pricing, monthly invoice, generous free credits to evaluate.
- Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools with monthly/annual commit, predictable throughput pricing, optional bursting for spikes.
- Redwood Private — platform license + deployment fees and support tiers for on-prem or VPC installs.

Pricing table (example guidance for prospect conversations):
Tier | Billing | Typical buyer | Quick talk track
--- | --- | --- | ---
Hosted | per-token / per-embedding | early-stage, dev/test | "Low friction to get started; pay only for what you use."
Dedicated | monthly/annual commit + usage | mid-market & enterprise | "Predictable unit economics and SLA-backed performance."
Private | license + deployment + support | regulated/enterprise | "Full control of network & keys; enterprise packaging for compliance."

Negotiation levers (commercial):
- Minimum commitment length (Dedicated) — longer terms reduce per-unit price.
- Burst capacity — short-term burst credits can be added to handle seasonal load.
- Observability retention add-on — useful for forensic and model debugging, billable separately.
- Professional services — migration, tuning & onboarding engagements.

Pricing objections & scripts:
- "Your per-token cost is higher than raw cloud VM costs." → "Raw GPU costs don’t include engineering time, optimizations, and reliability; we reduce per-effective-inference cost through batching, caching and runtime kernels, and we provide SRE-grade support and tools that teams typically build themselves."

5) Case Studies (concise, scannable)

Case Study A: FastCommerce (e-commerce conversational assistant)
- Profile: Series B startup, 80-engineer org, needs sub-150ms median response for search-assist and order workflows.
- Engagement: 8-week pilot on Hosted → Dedicated migration with reserved capacity.
- Outcome: 3x reduction in 95p latency after kernel and batching tuning; 40% reduction in per-100k-token cost vs prior self-hosted baseline; increased throughput to 3x during peak without service degradation.
- Assets: benchmark report link, before/after cost chart, SE tuning checklist.

Case Study B: LegalCloud (regulated vertical)
- Profile: Mid-market legal SaaS, required on-prem data residency and HSM-backed key management.
- Engagement: Private deployment + Professional Services for onboarding and compliance evidence.
- Outcome: Successful on-prem rollout with audit logs and KMS integration; enabled production RAG workflows with full data residency and SOC-like evidence for audits.
- Assets: deployment runbook, compliance evidence checklist.

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (short Q&A for initial conversations)

Q: Where does customer data reside when using Hosted?
A: By default, inference request data is stored transiently for operational telemetry and debugging. We offer data-retention controls, and sensitive workloads should use Dedicated or Private deployments; Hosted customers can opt into extended data deletion and redaction policies per contract.

Q: Do you support encryption-in-transit and at-rest?
A: Yes. We require TLS 1.2+ for in-transit. For at-rest, we use provider-managed encryption for hosted deployments and integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Dedicated and Private.

Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC/on-prem with customer-managed keys?
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages with KMS/HSM integration and full audit logging. We provide an onboarding playbook and professional services to validate the environment.

Q: What certifications / audits do you have?
A: We maintain an internal compliance tracker and provide SOC 2 Type II reports or ISO artifacts to qualifying customers under NDA or as part of an enterprise contract. Refer to security-and-compliance evidence pages for specifics.

Q: How is access controlled for engineers and support staff?
A: RBAC is enforced in the control plane. For Private deployments, role mappings can integrate with customer SSO (SAML/OIDC) and we support scoped access tokens for limited-purpose operations.

Q: How do you handle model updates and rollback for safety?
A: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback policies to earlier model variants. We recommend running eval prompt sets as part of CI to detect regressions before large rollouts.

7) Recommended Pilot (prescriptive scope)

Objective: Prove performance, cost, and operational readiness in 4 weeks.
Deliverables:
1. Week 0-1: Onboarding & integration — API integration, one representative endpoint, ingestion of sample prompts.
2. Week 1-2: Baseline benchmarking — run Redwood benchmark suite against customer's sample workload (latency percentiles, KV cache hit rate, token cost).
3. Week 2-3: Optimization & tuning — apply batching, quantization profile suggestions, and routing policies.
4. Week 3-4: Pilot validation — compare before/after metrics, present a short business case and recommended next steps (Dedicated sizing or Private packaging).

Pilot success criteria (example): median latency < 200ms for conversational flows, 95p latency < 500ms, and unit token cost reduction >= 25% vs current baseline.

8) Sales Assets (links & resources)

- Pitch deck templates: sales-deck-production-llms.pptx (internal)
- Benchmark report samples: benchmarks/llm-latency-cost-2026.pdf
- SE playbooks: se-tuning-checklist.md, dedicated-sizing-calculator.xlsx
- Security collateral: security-one-pager.pdf, SOC2-exec-summary.pdf (available under NDA)

Appendix — Example CLI snippets for SEs (share in technical follow-up)

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-claude-like-1","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

# Example config snippet for Dedicated sizing (YAML)
# (Include when sending dedicated proposal)
# gpu_pool: 8xA100, sequence_length_profile: short/medium, cache_enabled: true

Closing guidance for reps: Always qualify technical requirements (latency targets, throughput, data residency, KMS/HSM needs) before proposing Dedicated or Private. For initial demos prefer Hosted with realistic sample traffic to avoid surprises in the pilot.
